title: review: v2 review packets for fix rounds cover the whole lineage diff; fix-only approvals do not count for the merge
spec:
Reviews of fix rounds must cover the whole change, not only the fix commit.

Evidence 2026-10-06: the watchdog (T-1679 -> fix T-1682) and auto-merge (T-1678 -> fixes T-1681, T-1683) each reached
"approved" through reviews of a fix round only (T-1684, T-1685, T-1686); each review saw just the fix's diff (a test or
one prompt line) and said so, while ~700-900 lines of security-path code had never been reviewed. Independent full-diff
reviews then found 3 high-severity defects in each. A review spec that told the reviewer to read the full diff was
ignored because the packet showed only the fix diff.

Change orchestrator/spawn.py review_packet() (~line 1082) and whatever computes the diff range for a review of a task:
1. For a review whose input task has constraints.fix_round_for (follow the chain to the root execute task), the packet's
   diff is the whole lineage: from the merge-base with the goal branch (or origin/main when there is no goal branch) to
   the fix's head, i.e. everything that will land, not the fix commit alone. Keep the fix-only diff as a second, labelled
   section ("this round's change") when it fits.
2. If the lineage diff exceeds the packet budget, include the file list with per-file stats and the instruction to read
   the rest with `git diff <base>..<head> -- <file>`, naming the exact range; never silently truncate to the fix diff.
3. The daemon's review gate counts only reviews whose packet covered the lineage: stamp pipeline.review_range =
   "<base>..<head>" on the review task and, in merge_reviewed (daemon.py), ignore an approval whose review_range base is
   not the lineage base. Older reviews without the stamp count as today.
Tests in tests/test_spawn.py and tests/test_daemon.py: test_fix_round_review_packet_covers_lineage,
test_lineage_diff_over_budget_lists_files_and_range, test_merge_ignores_fix_only_approval,
test_plain_task_review_unchanged.


AMENDMENTS v2 from spec review T-1690 (final; sent to the builder without another spec review round; the post-gate
security review still applies). Where they differ from the text above, these win.
A1 Root cause: scoped_diff() ends with `-- *src["scope"]`, and a fix round's scope is narrow (one test, one prompt), so
   the packet filtered the lineage down to the fix's files. For a lineage review the path filter is the UNION of the
   scopes of every task in the chain (root execute task plus all fix rounds); if any scope is "**" or empty, no filter.
A2 No silent cut: for lineage reviews do not apply the [:40000] slice before building the packet. Build first a numstat
   file list (path, +/-) for the whole range, which always goes in; then hunks file by file within the packet budget;
   every file not shown in full is listed with the exact command `git diff <base>..<head> -- <file>`. New helper; leave
   bounded_diff for plain reviews.
A3 Ignored fix-only approval: merge_reviewed does not hold with "review state unknown"; it opens exactly one lineage
   review (through _open_reviews with lineage=True) and waits; only if that review fails or is held does the task hold,
   with the reason naming it.
A4 Stamping: _open_reviews stamps the review task at creation with lineage=True, review_base=<sha> and
   reviewed_sha=<head> (same moment reviewed_sha is stamped today); base = merge-base(goal/<parent> if it exists else
   origin/main, head). The packet builder reads these stamps and never recomputes them.
A5 Counting: an approval counts for a task with a fix_round chain only if the review has lineage=True and its
   reviewed_sha equals the task's current reviewed_sha. The base is not recomputed or compared.
A6 Chain failures (missing ancestor KeyError, cycle via a visited set, root without worktree, git merge-base failure):
   fall back to base = merge-base(origin/main, head) with no path filter and label the packet "lineage unresolved;
   reviewing the whole branch". Never fall back to a fix-only diff.
Extra tests: test_lineage_filter_is_union_of_chain_scopes, test_lineage_packet_numstat_always_present,
test_ignored_fix_only_approval_opens_lineage_review, test_stamp_at_open_reviews, test_chain_failure_reviews_whole_branch.
acceptance: the four named tests exist and pass
a review of a fix round shows origin/goal base..fix head, with the fix-only diff as a labelled extra section

result.summary: Lineage packet, stamping (lineage, review_base, reviewed_sha, pipeline.review_range), union-of-scopes filter, numstat-plus-expand-commands budgeting and the fix-only approval gate all match the spec and amendments A1-A6. I did not read the tests; the diff view showed 330 insertions and the tests are in the 408 lines I did not expand. The comments are minor.

comments.issue: The A3 early-return opens a review with n_reviews=1 and sets reviews_expected=1, even if the task's review_reason called for several reviews (a security path). That lowers the review count for security-path fix rounds. Confirm the single lineage review is on security_review_tier and that the reduction is intended.

The packet budget is 8000 chars, and the numstat file list always goes in unbounded. A large lineage can push the diff past the budget and leave the 'this round's change' section as an omitted-notice. That is allowed by the spec, but the reviewer may see no hunks at all, so consider a cap on the file list or a test for that case.
File paths from numstat go straight into the prompt's 'read with: git diff ...' lines. Filenames are untrusted and could carry injected text. This is low risk because the instructions are only hints.

When reviewed_sha is empty, the sha filter is skipped, so approvals are matched without the A5 reviewed_sha equality. That matches today's behaviour but weakens A5 for a fix-round task with no stamped sha.
